analysis: Reviewed the planner changes in ClusterPlacementPlanner.swift (head lines ~468-1335, plus the patch excerpt near 119-121 and 425-443) and the new `choice` field in ClusterTensorParallel.swift (patch lines 56-83). Both are local placement and performance-prediction logic. They add an optional `ClusterTensorParallelChoice` (.fastest) to the tensor-parallel family plan. A `fastest` family is ranked by the speed comparison, not by the tensor-parallel-first rule. When the link is unmeasured, it is priced with a conservative assumed reduction through `link.assuming(ClusterTensorParallelChoice.assumedReduction)` (evaluate(), head ~lines 636-643), not the forced keyed reduction. The visible diff has no new I/O, no network or crypto surface, and no change to authentication, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), cache storage (T-041) or key custody. Changes to the ClusterPlacement memory-fit logic (requirement/tensorRequirement) appear to be only context in the displayed excerpts. The new field decodes optionally, so older layouts read as before. A malicious layout could set `choice`, but layouts are already trusted inputs to the planner and it only shifts rank ordering. Open integration questions, none evidenced as security issues in the visible code: (1) whether `ClusterTensorParallelChoice` and `assumedReduction` (outside the supplied files) are defined safely, and how `link.assuming` marks the reduction as assumed/unkeyed. In `placeable`, `reduction.keyed || tensorParallelForAssessment` gates selection, so an assumed reduction marked keyed could let a TP mode be chosen without a measured keyed link. That is a correctness/performance concern and not a demonstrated security regression. (2) Placement still depends on the live load gate, which the code comments describe as authoritative, for actual memory admission. No finding.
